title: Pissaladiere
subtitle: A Nicoise onion tart with anchovies and black olives on a bread base
excerpt: Soft caramelised onions spread thickly over an olive oil bread base, finished with anchovy fillets laid in a lattice and black olives pushed into the gaps. The taste of Nice.
sourceNotes: Street food and home cooking staple from Nice and the surrounding area of the Cote d'Azur.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the onions up to two days ahead. The baked pissaladiere is best eaten the day it is made, warm or at room temperature.

content.text: Pissaladiere is built on a thick layer of very soft onions and a bread dough base, not a pastry case. The onions must be cooked until completely soft and slightly sweet. Do not rush this step or the result will taste raw and sharp.

Mix the flour, yeast, and salt in a bowl. Add the olive oil and lukewarm water. Mix to a soft dough, then knead on a floured surface for 8 minutes until smooth. Place in an oiled bowl, cover, and leave in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled.

While the dough proves, heat 4 tablespoons of olive oil in a large saucepan. Add the onions, thyme, and bay leaves. Cook over the lowest heat for 40 minutes, stirring every 5 to 10 minutes, until very soft and pale gold. Season with pepper. Discard the bay leaves and set aside to cool.
Heat the oven to 200C. Oil a large baking tray. Press and stretch the dough to fill the tray in a roughly 30 x 40cm rectangle, about 1cm thick.
Spread the cooked onions evenly over the dough, right to the edges.
Lay anchovy fillets across the surface in a diagonal lattice pattern. Press a black olive into each diamond of the lattice.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the base is golden and the edges are puffed and set.
Leave to cool for 5 minutes then cut into squares. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: The base is doughy and pale underneath.
items.cause: The oven was not hot enough, or the base was too thick.
items.fix: Preheat the baking tray in the oven and slide the pissaladiere onto it. Bake on the lowest shelf.

items.symptom: The onions taste sharp and bitter.
items.cause: They were not cooked long enough.
items.fix: Cook for a full 40 minutes at very low heat. They should be completely soft and have no raw smell.

items.symptom: The dough shrinks back when stretched.
items.cause: The gluten needs more time to relax.
items.fix: Let the dough rest for 5 minutes after each attempt to stretch it, then try again.
